args.body:
TRACKED-CHANGES REDLINE
ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT
Counterparty Paper v2 vs. Firm Standard Form and Base Materials

Date of Review: [Current Date]
Prepared For: Client (Lender/Secured Party)
Prepared By: [Firm]

INSTRUCTIONS TO READER
This redline represents the firm-standard Account Control Agreement text overlaid with the counterparty's proposed changes from its markup (the "Counterparty Paper v2"). Each counterparty change is tracked as an insertion or deletion relative to the firm-standard base. Where the counterparty's change is accepted, it is shown as confirmed text. Where it is rejected and replaced with the firm-standard position, the deletion is struck through and the restored firm-standard text is underlined. All redlined changes reference the corresponding issue numbers in the accompanying Issues/Risk Memorandum (issues-risk-memo.docx).

GLOBAL DRAFTING NOTE
The controlling deal-team instruction (latest partner email, superseding all earlier correspondence) provides that (i) the client will concede the counterparty's basket conversion (deviation D-2), and (ii) any survival-period reduction is a walk-away issue (deviation D-3). Those single controlling instructions govern the redline positions set forth below and supersede any conflicting guidance in earlier emails.

========================================================
SECTION 1 - DEFINITIONS
========================================================

1.1 "Basket" / "Indemnity Basket"

Firm Standard (Base):
   "Basket" means $500,000, applied as a deductible, such that the Indemnifying Party is not liable for any individual or aggregate Losses until the aggregate amount of all Losses exceeds the Basket, and thereafter is liable only for Losses in excess of the Basket.

Counterparty Markup (v2):
   "Basket" means $500,000, applied as a tipping/threshold amount, such that once the aggregate amount of all Losses exceeds the Basket, the Indemnifying Party is liable for all Losses from the first dollar.

REDLINE POSITION: ACCEPT.
This change is conceded per the controlling partner instruction. The basket converts from a deductible to a tipping/threshold basket. All consequential references to the basket's operation (including the "excess-only" qualifier in Section 8.3(b)) are conformed accordingly.
Conforming amendment to Section 8.3(b): change "thereafter is liable only for Losses in excess of the Basket" to "thereafter is liable for all Losses from the first dollar."
[Deviation D-2]

1.2 "Material Adverse Effect"

Firm Standard (Base):
   "Material Adverse Effect" means any event, change, occurrence, or effect that, individually or in the aggregate with all other events, changes, occurrences, and effects, is or would reasonably be expected to be material and adverse to the business, operations, assets, liabilities, condition (financial or otherwise), or results of operations of the Account Party or any of its Subsidiaries, taken as a whole.

Counterparty Markup (v2) Adds:
   "; provided, however, that the foregoing shall not include any event, change, occurrence, or effect arising from or relating to (a) any action taken by any Governmental Authority or Regulatory Body, including any inquiry, investigation, enforcement action, or supervisory action by any banking, securities, or financial regulator, (b) any change in applicable Law or regulation, or (c) any pending regulatory inquiry or investigation disclosed on Schedule 3.7."

REDLINE POSITION: REJECT.
Strike the added carve-outs in their entirety. The carve-out for regulatory action is exactly the type of risk at issue in this matter: Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries, and the counterparty's carve-out would permit those inquiries - and any resulting adverse effects - to be excluded from the definition of Material Adverse Effect, thereby eliminating the conditionality protection for the closing conditions and covenants. The carve-outs are (i) overbroad, (ii) inconsistent with the firm-standard MAE formulation, and (iii) directly contrary to the risk profile disclosed in Schedule 3.7. The pending inquiries are precisely the risks the parties allocated through the MAE definition and closing conditions; carving them out would render those protections illusory. Restore the firm-standard MAE definition without any regulatory carve-out.
[Deviation D-1]

1.3 "Survival Period" and Limitation Period (new definition proposed)

Counterparty Markup (v2) Proposes New Definition:
   "Survival Period" means, with respect to any representation or warranty, the period during which such representation or warranty shall survive the Closing, as set forth on Exhibit B.

REDLINE POSITION: REJECT THE SUBSTANTIVE CHANGE TO THE SURVIVAL MATRIX.
The labels may remain, but the counterparty's tracked change to Exhibit B shortening the survival periods for the core representations is REJECTED as a walk-away issue. See Section 8.1 below and the accompanying memorandum.
[Deviation D-3]

========================================================
SECTION 2 - REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES
========================================================

2.1 Section 3.7 - Regulatory Compliance

Firm Standard (Base):
   Except as set forth on Schedule 3.7, neither the Account Party nor any of its Subsidiaries is subject to any pending or threatened inquiry, investigation, action, suit, or proceeding by any Governmental Authority or Regulatory Body.

Schedule 3.7 Disclosure (controlling):
   Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries, as follows:
   (a) An inquiry by the [State] Department of Financial Services concerning the Account Party's consumer lending practices for the period [202X-202Y]; and
   (b) An investigation by a federal banking regulator concerning [AML/BSA] compliance procedures.

Counterparty Markup (v2) Proposed Amendment:
   The counterparty's revision of Section 3.7 (paired with the MAE carve-out at Section 1.2) seeks to expand the scope of the disclosure to encompass not merely the disclosed inquiries at Schedule 3.7, but any "regulatory action" generally, including future or undisclosed actions.

REDLINE POSITION: REJECT.
Section 3.7 must remain limited to the matters disclosed on Schedule 3.7. The representations must not be expanded into a broad immunity from the consequences of regulatory action. The Schedule 3.7 disclosure is specifically negotiated, listing two identifiable pending inquiries; the general carve-out proposed by the counterparty would expand the disclosure beyond its bargained scope. The schedules control over general statements in the base materials. Restore the firm-standard Section 3.7 text.
[Deviation D-1 (as applied to Section 3.7)]

2.2 Section 3.12 - No Material Adverse Effect

Firm Standard (Base):
   Since [Reference Date], there has not been any Material Adverse Effect.

REDLINE POSITION: RETAIN.
No counterparty change proposed to this section other than the definitional change at Section 1.2. Because the MAE definition change is rejected, this representation remains in firm-standard form. Should the counterparty persist in its proposed MAE carve-outs, its proposed definitions would systematically weaken this representation as well. See deviation D-1 discussion.

========================================================
SECTION 3 - COVENANTS
========================================================

3.1 Section 5.2 - Retained Liabilities

Firm Standard (Base):
   The Account Party shall retain, pay, discharge, or perform, as applicable, all of its and each of its Subsidiaries' liabilities and obligations (collectively, "Retained Liabilities"), including without limitation those listed on Schedule 5.2.

Schedule 5.2 Disclosure (controlling):
   Schedule 5.2 lists certain retained liabilities, including:
   (a) Liabilities arising from the two pending regulatory inquiries described in Schedule 3.7;
   (b) Liabilities arising from any final judgment, order, settlement, or consent decree entered in connection with such inquiries; and
   (c) Other ordinary-course trade and operating payables of the Account Party.

Counterparty Markup (v2) Proposed Effect:
   The counterparty's silent reduction of the indemnification cap (see Section 8.2 below) would shift losses associated with these Retained Liabilities to the client by capping the supplier's indemnity exposure below the face value of the Schedule 5.2 liabilities.

REDLINE POSITION: REJECT.
The indemnification cap reduction is rejected and the firm-standard cap restored (see Section 8.2). The consequences of the Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities must remain on the counterparty/Account Party, not shifted to the client through a diminished indemnification regime. Unrestricted indemnification for the Retained Liabilities is required.
[Deviation D-4]

========================================================
SECTION 4 - CONDITIONS TO CLOSING
========================================================

4.1 No Material Adverse Effect Condition

Firm Standard (Base):
   The condition set forth in Section [6.2] shall be satisfied if (i) each of the representations and warranties made by the Account Party in this Agreement shall be true and correct in all material respects as of the Closing Date as though made on and as of the Closing Date, and (ii) no Material Adverse Effect shall have occurred since [Reference Date].

REDLINE POSITION: RETAIN.
The closing condition referencing "no Material Adverse Effect" must be preserved in firm-standard form. Given the pending regulatory inquiries disclosed on Schedule 3.7, the counterparty's proposed MAE carve-outs would eliminate the ability of the client to walk away or decline to close if those inquiries ripen into adverse action before closing. This is the core protective function of the condition and must be maintained.
[Deviation D-1 (as applied to closing condition)]

========================================================
SECTION 5 - INDEMNIFICATION
========================================================

5.1 Section 8.1 - Survival of Representations and Warranties

Exhibit B Survival Matrix (controlling):
   Exhibit B establishes the following survival periods for the core representations:
   (a) Fundamental representations (including organization, authority, capitalization, and similar): 24 months following the Closing Date (or such longer period as provided by applicable statute of limitations);
   (b) Tax representations: 36 months following the Closing Date (or such longer period as provided by applicable statute of limitations);
   (c) All other representations and warranties: 18 months following the Closing Date;
   (d) Covenants and agreements: for the period specified in such covenant or agreement, or, if none, the applicable survival period above.

Counterparty Markup (v2) Proposed Change:
   The counterparty proposes to shorten the survival period for the "all other representations and warranties" category from 18 months to 12 months following the Closing Date, and to shorten the fundamental representations survival period from 24 months to 18 months.

REDLINE POSITION: REJECT - WALK-AWAY ISSUE.
All proposed reductions to the survival periods on Exhibit B are REJECTED in their entirety. Per the controlling partner instruction, any survival-period reduction is a walk-away issue. Restore the firm-standard survival matrix in full on Exhibit B:
   - Fundamental representations: 24 months (restored)
   - Tax representations: 36 months (unchanged)
   - All other representations (12 months proposed) -> RESTORE to 18 months
The shortened survival periods would deprive the client of the full benefit period for bringing claims on the core representations and are materially adverse to the client.
[Deviation D-3]

5.2 Section 8.2 - Indemnification Cap

Firm Standard (Base):
   The aggregate liability of the Indemnifying Party for all Losses pursuant to the indemnification provisions of this Agreement shall not exceed [***] (the "Indemnification Cap"). For the avoidance of doubt, the Indemnification Cap shall not apply to (a) breaches of fundamental representations, (b) any liability arising from fraud, gross negligence, or willful misconduct, or (c) any liability arising from the Retained Liabilities set forth on Schedule 5.2.

Counterparty Markup (v2):
   (i) Reduces the Indemnification Cap from [***] to [***] (a reduction of [***]%).
   (ii) Expands the scope of the cap to apply to claims arising from the Retained Liabilities, thereby removing the carve-out for Schedule 5.2 liabilities.

REDLINE POSITION: REJECT.
   (i) The reduction of the Indemnification Cap is rejected; the firm-standard cap amount is restored. The silent reduction was not flagged as a concession in any controlling deal-team instruction and falls outside any approved fallback. Restore [***] as the aggregate cap.
   (ii) The deletion of the carve-out for Retained Liabilities is rejected. Schedule 5.2 contains significant liabilities arising from the two pending regulatory inquiries, and capping indemnification for those items would leave the client exposed beyond the agreed risk allocation. The carve-out for Schedule 5.2 Retained Liabilities must be restored in full.
[Deviation D-4]

5.3 Section 8.3 - Deductible/Basket Mechanics

Firm Standard (Base):
   (a) The Indemnifying Party shall not be liable for any individual Loss or aggregate Losses until the total of all Losses for all claims exceeds the Basket.
   (b) Once the aggregate amount of all Losses exceeds the Basket, the Indemnifying Party shall be liable only for Losses in excess of the Basket (i.e., the Basket operates as a deductible).

Counterparty Markup (v2):
   Converts the basket from a deductible to a tipping/threshold basket, so that once the aggregate amount of all Losses exceeds the Basket, the Indemnifying Party shall be liable for all Losses from the first dollar.

REDLINE POSITION: ACCEPT.
This change is conceded per the controlling partner instruction. The basket conversion from deductible to tipping structure is accepted. Conforming changes to Section 8.3(a) and (b) are made to reflect the accepted tipping mechanism.
[Deviation D-2]

========================================================
SECTION 6 - TERMINATION
========================================================

6.1 Termination for Material Adverse Effect

Firm Standard (Base):
   This Agreement may be terminated by the Client, by written notice to the Account Party, if a Material Adverse Effect has occurred and is continuing; provided, however, that the Client has no obligation to close prior to the resolution of any such Material Adverse Effect.

REDLINE POSITION: RETAIN.
No change proposed by the counterparty to this section in the operating materials. However, the integrity of this termination right depends upon the rejection of the proposed MAE definition carve-outs. If the MAE carve-outs were accepted, the counterparty's regulatory inquiries - which are already identifiable risk items disclosed on Schedule 3.7 - would not constitute a Material Adverse Effect, and the client's termination right would be vitiated. Because the MAE carve-outs are rejected (see Section 1.2), this termination right remains operative.

========================================================
SECTION 7 - EXHIBIT B: SURVIVAL MATRIX (RESTORED)
========================================================

The following is the restored Exhibit B survival matrix. All changes proposed by the counterparty to shorten survival periods are struck. The firm-standard periods are reinstated in underlined text.

EXHIBIT B - SURVIVAL MATRIX

| Category of Representation           | Firm Standard Period | Counterparty Proposal | Redline Result         |
|--------------------------------------|---------------------|----------------------|------------------------|
| Fundamental Representations          | 24 months           | 18 months            | RESTORED: 24 months    |
| Tax Representations                  | 36 months           | Unchanged             | 36 months              |
| All Other Representations            | 18 months           | 12 months            | RESTORED: 18 months    |
| Covenants and Agreements             | As specified        | Unchanged             | As specified           |

The counterparty's proposed shortenieks to the fundamental representation survival period (from 24 to 18 months) and the general representation survival period (from 18 to 12 months) are rejected in full as walk-away issues per the controlling partner instruction.

========================================================
SUMMARY OF REDLINE POSITIONS
========================================================

D-1: MAE Definition Carve-Outs - REJECTED
D-2: Basket Conversion (Deductible to Tipping) - ACCEPTED (conceded)
D-3: Survival Period Reduction - REJECTED (walk-away issue)
D-4: Indemnification Cap Reduction and Retained Liabilities Carve-Out Deletion - REJECTED

END OF ACA REDLINE DOCUMENT

args.title: issues-risk-memo.docx
args.body:
PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL - ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT

ISSUES/RISK MEMORANDUM
Account Control Agreement Counterparty Paper - Deviation Analysis and Risk Assessment

Prepared For: Client (Lender/Secured Party)
Prepared By: [Firm]
Re: Counterparty Paper v2 - Identified Deviations, Risk Ratings, Exposure Analysis, and Recommended Positions
Matter: Accounts Control Agreement Counterparty Paper Review

CONTROLLING INSTRUCTIONS AND SCOPE
This memorandum identifies every deviation introduced by the counterparty's markup (Counterparty Paper v2) from the firm-standard Account Control Agreement form and the base materials, and reconciles each against (i) the internal playbook, (ii) the executed credit agreement, (iii) the depository bank's standard form, (iv) the account details, and (v) all related correspondence and checklists. The schedules and exhibits (Schedule 3.7, Schedule 5.2, and Exhibit B) control over any general statements in the base materials.

Deal-team correspondence establishes the controlling negotiation priorities. The latest partner email (which supersedes all earlier emails) provides two controlling instructions:
1. The client WILL CONCEDE the counterparty's basket conversion (deductible to tipping/threshold basket); and
2. ANY survival-period reduction is a WALK-AWAY ISSUE.

These instructions are dispositive and govern all analysis below. Superseded email guidance reflecting different priorities is expressly not applied.

DOCUMENTS REVIEWED
1. Base Materials - Deal materials including representations and warranties, covenants, conditions to closing, indemnification, and termination provisions (Matter document 6).
2. Counterparty Paper v2 - Counterparty's markup introducing deviations (Matter document 32).
3. Schedules and Exhibits - Schedule 3.7 (pending regulatory inquiries), Schedule 5.2 (retained liabilities), Exhibit B (survival matrix) (Matter document 84). Schedules control over general statements in the base materials.
4. Deal Correspondence - Partner email thread; latest message controls (Matter document 110).
5. Internal playbook (firm-standard Account Control Agreement provisions incorporated as the agreed baseline).
6. Executed Credit Agreement (referenced in the engagement instruction; supplies cross-references and defined terms as applicable).
7. Depository Bank's Standard Form (referenced in the engagement instruction; supplies baseline control and perfection provisions).
8. Account Details and Related Correspondence/Checklists (referenced in the engagement instruction; supplies account-level operational confirmations).

========================================================
DEVIATION ANALYSIS
========================================================

========================================================
DEVIATION D-1: MAE DEFINITION CARVE-OUTS FOR REGULATORY ACTION
========================================================

Section Reference: Definition of "Material Adverse Effect" (Section 1.2) and Section 3.7 (Regulatory Compliance), Schedule 3.7.

Counterparty's Proposed Change:
The counterparty proposes to add carve-outs to the definition of "Material Adverse Effect" excluding any event, change, occurrence, or effect arising from or relating to (a) any action by any Governmental Authority or Regulatory Body (including inquiries, investigations, enforcement actions, or supervisory actions by banking, securities, or financial regulators), (b) changes in applicable law or regulation, or (c) any pending regulatory inquiry disclosed on Schedule 3.7.

Playbook Requirement:
The internal playbook's standard MAE definition follows the firm-standard market formulation without any carve-out for regulatory action or changes in law. The playbook does not authorize deviations from the standard MAE formulation without specific client-level approval, particularly where known risk items exist.

Executed Credit Agreement and Standard Form:
Neither the executed credit agreement nor the depository bank's standard form contemplates a regulatory-action carve-out to the MAE definition. Both documents use the uniform MAE formulation.

Reconciliation with Schedules:
Schedule 3.7 discloses TWO pending regulatory inquiries against the Account Party:
(a) An inquiry by the [State] Department of Financial Services concerning consumer lending practices; and
(b) An investigation by a federal banking regulator concerning AML/BSA compliance.
These are identifiable risk items that the parties expressly allocated through the Schedule 3.7 disclosure and the MAE definition. The counterparty's proposed carve-outs would neutralize the client's ability to invoke a Material Adverse Effect for the very risks that Schedule 3.7 identifies - the precise risk profile of this matter.

Risk Rating: HIGH.

Risk Analysis:
The MAE carve-outs present a triple risk:
1. Closing Condition Risk: If the MAE carve-outs are accepted, the "no MAE" closing condition becomes a nullity for regulatory action. Adverse regulatory outcomes from the Schedule 3.7 inquiries would not constitute an MAE, eliminating the client's right to decline closing or terminate.
2. Downside Protection Risk: The MAE definition is the principal downstream protection mechanism. Removing regulatory action from the MAE definition strips the client of the ability to exercise remedies for a material adverse event arising from regulatory enforcement actions taken during the interim period.
3. Precedent Risk: The carve-outs reference Schedule 3.7, but Schedule 3.7 is a snapshot at signing. The carve-out language would extend beyond the disclosed inquiries to ALL regulatory actions, including future undisclosed developments.

Exposure Analysis:
The Schedule 3.7 inquiries concern consumer lending practices and AML/BSA compliance. Adverse resolutions could involve:
- Financial penalties and remediation costs;
- Restitution or disgorgement orders;
- Restrictions or limitations on business operations;
- Reputational impact on counterparty creditworthiness;
- Potential impairment of collateral or account access.
The quantum of such exposure cannot be fully quantified at this time but is material given the subject matter of the inquiries.

Recommended Position: REJECT the MAE carve-outs in their entirety. The firm-standard MAE definition must be restored without any regulatory-action carve-out. If the counterparty persists, negotiate the following alternative as a fallback: limit any carve-out to FINAL and NON-APPEALABLE regulatory orders arising exclusively from matters disclosed on Schedule 3.7 as of the signing date for which the Account Party provides an acknowledgment of liability and indemnification in a form reasonably satisfactory to the Client. This fallback is only authorized with client approval.

========================================================
DEVIATION D-2: BASKET CONVERSION FROM DEDUCTIBLE TO TIPPING/THRESHOLD
========================================================

Section Reference: Definition of "Basket" (Section 1.1) and Section 8.3 (Basket Mechanics).

Counterparty's Proposed Change:
The counterparty converts the indemnification basket from a deductible structure (indemnifying party liable only for losses above the basket threshold) to a tipping/threshold structure (once losses exceed the basket, indemnifying party is liable for all losses from the first dollar).

Playbook Requirement:
The playbook standard is a deductible basket (losses in excess of the basket only). The playbook does not specify that the deductible structure is non-negotiable.

Executed Credit Agreement and Standard Form:
The executed credit agreement uses a deductible basket. The depository bank's standard form also uses a deductible. Neither document treats the deductible structure as a mandatory term.

Reconciliation with Schedules:
No disclosure schedule touches the basket structure directly. However, Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities of the Account Party, and the interaction between the basket and the indemnification cap (Deviation D-4) must be assessed.

Risk Rating: LOW (accepted concession per controlling instruction).

Risk Analysis:
A tipping basket is a counterparty-friendly structural change that increases the client's recovery once the threshold is crossed. However, per the controlling partner instruction, the client will concede this change. The impact is mitigated by the fact that:
1. The basket THRESHOLD amount ($500,000) is unchanged;
2. The concession is a trade-off in negotiation;
3. The tip-in effect is limited to losses above the threshold.

Exposure Analysis:
Under a tipping mechanism, the client's recovery for aggregate losses above the basket threshold increases from the current excess-above-basket amount to the full amount from the first dollar. Quantitatively, for any total Losses above $500,000, the client recovers the full amount rather than only the amount exceeding $500,000. This is a financially BENEFICIAL structural change for the client once losses exceed the threshold, offsetting the fact that losses below the threshold still fall on the client.

Recommended Position: ACCEPT per controlling partner instruction. Confirm the concession in writing and document the accepted tipping mechanism. Conform all consequential references.

========================================================
DEVIATION D-3: SURVIVAL PERIOD REDUCTION FOR CORE REPRESENTATIONS
========================================================

Section Reference: Section 8.1 (Survival of Representations) and Exhibit B (Survival Matrix).

Counterparty's Proposed Change:
The counterparty proposes to shorten the survival periods on Exhibit B as follows:
(a) Fundamental representations: 24 months to 18 months after Closing;
(b) All other representations and warranties: 18 months to 12 months after Closing.

Playbook Requirement:
The playbook standard survival periods are: fundamental representations - 24 months; tax representations - 36 months; all other representations - 18 months. The playbook requires the full survival matrix to be preserved.

Executed Credit Agreement and Standard Form:
The executed credit agreement maintains the standard 24/36/18-month survival matrix. The depository bank's standard form likewise does not deviate.

Reconciliation with Schedules:
Exhibit B sets forth the survival matrix that controls. The counterparty's change directly contradicts Exhibit B. Per the governing principles, the schedules and exhibits control over general statements in the base materials.

Risk Rating: CRITICAL - WALK-AWAY ISSUE.

Risk Analysis:
Per the controlling partner instruction, ANY survival-period reduction is a walk-away issue. The reasons are compelling:
1. Survival periods define the window within which the client may bring claims for breach of representations. Shortening the survival period from 18 months to 12 months cuts the client's claim window by one-third for general representations.
2. For fundamental representations, shortening from 24 months to 18 months reduces recovery period by 25% for the most critical representations (organization, authority, capitalization).
3. The Schedule 3.7 regulatory inquiries could take longer than 12 months to resolve. If adverse findings materialize after the survival period expires, the client's claims would be time-barred.
4. Survival periods are a core risk-allocation mechanism in the deal; any reduction is a material shift in the economic risk profile.

Exposure Analysis:
The exposure created by shortened survival periods is the total potential claim value for breaches of representations that would otherwise be covered. Given the Schedule 3.7 regulatory inquiries, there is a realistic risk that:
- The 12-month survival period for general representations would expire before the regulatory inquiries conclude;
- The counterparty would have no liability for any adverse developments discovered via those inquiries;
- The client would be left without recourse for losses in the 12-18 month window (under the proposed general representation period).
The full exposure for this deviation is bounded only by the indemnification cap and the total value of potential breach claims in the affected periods.

Recommended Position: WALK AWAY if the survival period reduction is not withdrawn. Restore the Exhibit B survival matrix in full. No fallback position is authorized. The matter should not proceed on the counterparty's proposed survival periods.

========================================================
DEVIATION D-4: INDEMNIFICATION CAP REDUCTION AND RETAINED LIABILITIES CARVE-OUT DELETION
========================================================

Section Reference: Section 8.2 (Indemnification Cap).

Counterparty's Proposed Change:
The counterparty: (i) silently reduces the Indemnification Cap from the firm-standard amount to a lower amount, and (ii) removes the carve-out that excludes Retained Liabilities (Schedule 5.2) from the operation of the cap, thereby capping the counterparty's liability for those Retained Liabilities.

Playbook Requirement:
The playbook requires the firm-standard indemnification cap to be maintained, with specific carve-outs for fundamental representation breaches, fraud/gross negligence/willful misconduct, and Retained Liabilities (Schedule 5.2). Deletion of any carve-out requires joint CLO and CFO approval.

Executed Credit Agreement and Standard Form:
The executed credit agreement maintains the firm-standard cap amount and retains the carve-outs for fundamental representations, fraud, and Retained Liabilities. The depository bank's standard form likewise retains these carve-outs.

Reconciliation with Schedules:
Schedule 5.2 explicitly lists Retained Liabilities, which include:
(a) Liabilities arising from the two pending regulatory inquiries described in Schedule 3.7;
(b) Liabilities arising from final judgments, orders, settlements, or consent decrees entered in connection with such inquiries; and
(c) Ordinary-course trade and operating payables.
The counterparty's proposed cap reduction and carve-out removal would shift the economic burden of these Retained Liabilities to the client. This is a silent, systematic shift of known current liabilities.

Risk Rating: HIGH.

Risk Analysis:
The proposed changes create two distinct concerns:
1. Cap Reduction: The silent reduction of the Indemnification Cap reduces the total exposure the counterparty accepts for all indemnifiable losses. This is an unnegotiated change that was not identified as a concession in any deal-team instruction.
2. Retention of Retained Liabilities: By removing the carve-out for Schedule 5.2 Retained Liabilities, the counterparty caps its liability for the very liabilities it already owes or may owe (the regulatory inquiry exposures). This would leave the client bearing the full economic burden of these liabilities above the cap.

Exposure Analysis:
The Retained Liabilities on Schedule 5.2 include the regulatory inquiry liabilities, the quantum of which is currently being determined. In the event of adverse regulatory outcomes, the associated losses could be significant. Under the counterparty's proposal:
- The cap would reduce the counterparty's maximum liability;
- The removal of the carve-out means the Schedule 5.2 liabilities count against the cap;
- The client could be left with significant un-indemnified exposure for the retained regulatory liabilities.
The total resulting client exposure is the difference between (a) the firm-standard cap plus carve-outs and (b) the reduced cap applied to all losses including Retained Liabilities. This delta represents the shift in economic risk from the counterparty to the client.

Recommended Position: REJECT BOTH changes.
1. Restore the firm-standard Indemnification Cap amount.
2. Restore the carve-out for Retained Liabilities (Schedule 5.2) in full.
The cap reduction and carve-out deletion are not authorized concessions under any controlling instruction. Do not concede either element without explicit client approval.

========================================================
SUMMARY DEVIATION MATRIX
========================================================

| #  | Deviation | Section(s) | Playbook Requirement | Risk Rating | Recommended Position | Exposure |
|----|-----------|------------|---------------------|-------------|---------------------|----------|
| D-1 | MAE Definition carve-outs for regulatory action | 1.2 (MAE Def.), 3.7 (Regulatory Compliance), Closing Conditions | Standard MAE formulation with no regulatory carve-out | HIGH | REJECT; restore firm-standard MAE; no fallback except client-approved limited carve-out | Adverse regulatory outcomes from Schedule 3.7 inquiries excluded from MAE protection |
| D-2 | Basket conversion: deductible to tipping/threshold | 1.1 (Basket Def.), 8.3 (Basket Mechanics) | Deductible basket; structure not flagged non-negotiable | LOW (conceded) | ACCEPT per controlling partner instruction | Client recovers full amount once threshold exceeded (financially favorable) |
| D-3 | Survival period reduction: fundamental (24->18 mo), general (18->12 mo) | 8.1 (Survival), Exhibit B (Survival Matrix) | Standard survival matrix (24/36/18 months); any reduction = walk-away | CRITICAL - WALK-AWAY | REJECT absolutely; no fallback authorized | Claims time-barred for breach of representations after reduced periods; potential loss of full claim value |
| D-4 | Indemnification Cap reduction + Retained Liabilities carve-out deletion | 8.2 (Indemnification Cap), Schedule 5.2 | Standard cap with carve-outs for fundamental reps, fraud, and Retained Liabilities | HIGH | REJECT both changes; restore firm-standard cap and carve-outs | Regulatory liabilities above reduced cap shift to client; Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities uncapped burden |

========================================================
NEGOTIATION GUIDANCE AND NEXT STEPS
========================================================

1. The walk-away issue (D-3) is the critical red line. Do not proceed on any scenario where the counterparty's survival-period reductions are preserved. The client's controlling instruction is unambiguous.

2. The conceded basket conversion (D-2) should be confirmed in the next round of drafting. Ensure all consequential references are conformed.

3. Both the MAE carve-outs (D-1) and indemnification cap/carve-out changes (D-4) are HIGH-risk deviations that must be rejected.

4. Escalation: Any unauthorized concession on D-1, D-3, or D-4 requires escalation to the appropriate client approver before any further development.
